Yes. The Codex failure is real, and I found the concrete reason.

It is not a “merge today broke cleanup” issue. It is a content-overlap bug in our carry-forward logic, triggered by Codex’s second-turn edit flow under `core.autocrlf=true` in E2E setup at [repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/e2e/testutil/repo.go#L64).

What happened in the failing run:
- On the second prompt, Codex first patched `src/main.go`, then unexpectedly ran `git checkout -- src/main.go`, then patched it again. You can see that in [console.log](/tmp/codex-run-24235994055/2026-04-10T09-22-18/TestPartialStaging-codex/console.log#L145) and [console.log](/tmp/codex-run-24235994055/2026-04-10T09-22-18/TestPartialStaging-codex/console.log#L170).
- That checkout rewrote the file with CRLF line endings. The diff output shows the line-ending flip explicitly at [console.log](/tmp/codex-run-24235994055/2026-04-10T09-22-18/TestPartialStaging-codex/console.log#L173).
- Because the repo has `core.autocrlf=true`, `git add -A` normalized the staged/committed blob back to LF, but the working tree still had the mixed-line-ending version.
- Our carry-forward check in [content_overlap.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/content_overlap.go#L493) calls [workingTreeMatchesCommit](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/content_overlap.go#L522), which compares raw on-disk bytes to the commit blob hash. That is too strict when Git EOL filters are active.

The failing log confirms exactly that:
- `commit_hash:"392a661"` and `shadow_hash:"ecccdfd"` at [entire.log](/tmp/codex-run-24235994055/2026-04-10T09-22-18/TestPartialStaging-codex/entire-logs/entire.log#L118)
- then `remaining:["src/main.go"]` and carry-forward happens at [entire.log](/tmp/codex-run-24235994055/2026-04-10T09-22-18/TestPartialStaging-codex/entire-logs/entire.log#L120)

I verified those hashes:
- `392a661...` is the LF version of the final file
- `ecccdfd...` is the mixed CRLF/LF version Codex left in the worktree

So the real bug is in our cleanup heuristic, not in shadow-branch deletion itself. We are treating “worktree bytes differ from commit blob after Git’s clean/smudge filters” as “uncommitted agent changes remain.”

The likely fix is to stop using raw blob hashing in `workingTreeMatchesCommit` and instead ask Git whether the path is actually dirty relative to the current commit/index, so EOL normalization does not create phantom carry-forward.

If you want, I can patch that next and add a regression test for this exact Codex + `autocrlf` case.
